newsitem.title: USA: Coastal seen staying the course - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Coastal seen staying the course - analysts.

text.p: Coastal Corp Chairman Oscar Wyatt's planned retirement later this year caps a smooth transition to a younger management team at the Houston-based diversified energy company, analysts said on Tuesday.

Wyatt, a legend in the U.S. oil industry, said he would hand over the reins of the company he founded more than 40 years ago to President and Chief Executive Officer David Arledge, his hand-picked successor, on July 15.
"This is just the final piece, but he's been moving in this direction for some time," Smith Barney analyst Dan Tulis said. "It will be viewed as a changing of the guard."

Arledge is widely credited with bolstering Coastal's exploration and production operations in recent years while building up its international power operations and running the company's day-to-day operations.
"Dave and Oscar were cut from the same cloth," PaineWebber analyst Ron Barone said of the "hard driving, focused" executives. "I don't think there's any major change at all."
Wyatt, 72, will continue to hold sway with the company as a director and chairman of the executive committee, and he remains Coastal's largest single shareholder, analysts noted.

"He's been a tremendous force in terms of growing the company and I respect him. On the other hand, I guess (his retirement) kind of signals a major transition in the management of Coastal. Coastal and Oscar Wyatt have been intertwined forever," Tulis said.
